entities.name: Notch2
observations: In hepatic Notch2 conditional knockout mice, fetal and neonatal livers lacked CK19-, DBA-, and SOX9-positive ductal structures; secondary cholangiocyte differentiation and duct formation began around weaning despite persistent Notch2 deficiency.

entities.name: Notch2 duct agenesis
observations: Notch2fl/fl;Alfp-Cretg/- mice showed absent fetal/neonatal intrahepatic duct markers, supporting perinatal bile-duct agenesis; secondary, disorganized ducts formed beginning around weaning, with some connecting to extrahepatic ducts.
Approximately 30% of cKO mice were no longer jaundiced by 6 months; postnatal cholangiocytes lacked nuclear NOTCH2, arguing against rescue by unrecombined Notch2-positive cells.

entities.name: PMID:25446530
observations: Primary Developmental Biology study titled “Hepatic Notch2 deficiency leads to bile duct agenesis perinatally and secondary bile duct formation after weaning.”

entities.name: PMID:23500150
observations: Separate liver-specific Notch2 deficiency study during DDC or ANIT biliary injury; progenitors accumulated but failed to mature into biliary ducts, addressing repair rather than perinatal agenesis and post-weaning developmental rescue.
